subject: Deployment mode recommendation and next steps — Hosted fallback / Dedicated proposal
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@brightdata.com>, Maya Reed <maya.reed@brightdata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + proposed checklist (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Hi Tom / Maya,

Thanks again for a productive call this morning — appreciated the clear context about BrightData's inference surface. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can scope a recommendation: 

Summary of what I captured from the call:
- Workload: realtime scoring for enrichment pipeline (per-request prompt -> 1-2 short responses)
- Expected steady QPS: ~250–400; peak QPS: ~1.8k during batch backfills
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end <= 75 ms (ideally <= 50 ms for priority flows)
- Typical prompt length: 120 tokens; response length: 40–120 tokens
- KV cache friendliness: high (many repeated prefixes)
- Data residency: US, not air-gapped; SOC 2 required, no on-prem at P0

To confirm before we lock a recommendation: can you confirm the following items?
1) Concurrency pattern: are requests coming from many small clients (hundreds of clients each at low qps) or a few large ingestion workers?
2) Are there hard SLA windows for the 50 ms target (e.g., checkout flows), or is that an aspirational internal goal?
3) Any regulatory need for in-region-only private endpoints (VPC) beyond SOC 2?

Attached is a simple SLA & throughput matrix I suggested during the call — it lists where Hosted should comfortably cover you and when Dedicated starts to make economic and latency sense. Also attaching our high-level Dedicated pricing PDF so you have a starting point.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm the three items above (1–3) — if you like, a short reply with bullet answers is perfect.
- If the latency target is firm, we'll propose either a Dedicated pilot (reserved GPU pool + test harness) or a Hosted pilot with routing + KV caching enabled to validate p95 at expected qps.
- I'll loop in Marcus (solutions eng) to propose a minimal pilot test plan and the hardware profile.

Would you prefer we propose a Dedicated pilot first, or run a low-friction Hosted pilot to validate the traffic characteristics?

Thanks —

Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0194
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@brightdata.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Reed <maya.reed@brightdata.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + proposed checklist (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Thanks Jasmine — great summary. Answers below: 

1) Concurrency pattern: mostly many small clients. We have ~1,200 edge agents that fan in; each agent is low qps (sub-1 qps) but they aggregate through a handful of regional ingress clusters. Peak traffic comes from batch enrichment runs initiated from 10 controller nodes.

2) Latency: the <= 50 ms is a hard SLA for the checkout scoring path (we can route a subset of traffic marked "priority"). The 75 ms number is our broader p95 target for all scoring. Prioritization is feasible in the request headers (we can tag).

3) Residency: SOC 2 is required. No additional region restrictions beyond US. No on-prem requirement at this stage.

We prefer a quick pilot that proves p95 at our average steady qps (~300) for both priority and normal traffic. If Dedicated buys us consistent 50 ms p95 for priority, we are open to a reserved pilot — but we'd like to see cost delta and a performance validation plan first.

Also: can you confirm whether Redwood's Hosted tier supports explicit per-request priority routing + KV cache affinity today, or would that require a custom config?

Tom
VP, Platform Engineering | BrightData Inc.
Tom.Alvarez@brightdata.com

Subject: Internal: BrightData pilot ask — TL;DR and proposal

Marcus / Marissa,

TL;DR from Tom: steady ~300 qps (many small clients), peaks ~1.8k during backfills, strict p95<=50ms for a tagged priority subset; SOC 2; US-only. They want a pilot that proves p95 at steady qps, then evaluate Dedicated if cost/perf justify.

Initial read / constraints:
- Hosted: with request-priority routing + KV prefix caching + continuous batching tuned for short responses, I think we can meet ~75 ms p95 easily and plausibly hit 50–60 ms p95 for many cases. However, at ~300 steady qps with bursts to ~1.8k, tails could widen unless we isolate capacity.
- Dedicated: gives predictable tail latency because of reserved GPU pools and pinned model instances / kernel configs. More operational setup but will almost certainly deliver consistent sub-50 ms p95 for priority flows if we size the pool correctly.

Recommendation for pilot (two-phase):
Phase A — Hosted quick-proof (2 weeks):
- Enable per-request priority header routing into a priority queue.
- Turn on KV prefix caching and configure continuous batching with tight latency SLOs (max batch delay 5 ms).
- Run at steady ~300 qps for 72 hours with synthetic traffic that mirrors their agent fan-in shape; collect p50/p95/p99 per-route.
- Goal: measurable p95 <= 75 ms; aim to see if priority subset can get to 50–60 ms.

Phase B — Dedicated sizing trial (1–2 weeks) if Phase A shows tail risk or we hit warm GPU inefficiencies:
- Propose a small reserved pool (estimate: 2 x A100-equivalent nodes with optimized kernels, or 4 x A10-equivalent depending on model quantization) to validate sub-50 ms p95 for priority.
- Provide a cost comparison and projected monthly spend versus running Hosted at required SLAs.

Questions for Marcus (technical): can you sketch the minimal test harness and a rough Dedicated pod size estimate (A100 vs A10 equiv) assuming their model is a ~7B LLM quantized to int8? Also, does Redwood Hosted today support explicit per-request priority queues + KV affinity out of the box or is that a config we need to build?

If you agree, I'll reply to Tom with the phased plan and ask for approval to start Phase A. I think this approach minimizes cost friction while giving BrightData a clear path to Dedicated if the tails require it.

— Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 19:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: BrightData pilot ask — TL;DR and proposal

On Thu, Apr 29, 2027 at 6:30 PM Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marcus / Marissa,
>
> TL;DR from Tom: steady ~300 qps (many small clients), peaks ~1.8k during backfills, strict p95<=50ms for a tagged priority subset; SOC 2; US-only.

Thanks — good summary. Quick answers and action items: 

1) Hosted capabilities: yes — we support per-request priority tags and have KV cache affinity and routing controls in the Console today. The priority queue configs are exposed in Dedicated customers but are also available as advanced options for Hosted (we'll need to flip a config flag and provide a short runbook). Continuous batching with max delay knobs is supported in both Hosted and Dedicated runtime.

2) Rough Dedicated sizing (assumes a 7B int8 model, 120 token prompts + 80 token responses):
- Conservative: 2 x A100-equivalents (higher perf) should give sustained low p95 (<45 ms) for the priority subset and handle bursts with headroom.
- Cost-efficient: 4 x A10-equivalents could hit ~50–60 ms p95 depending on kernel choices and batching windows; cheaper but closer to the limit.

3) Test harness: I can assemble a small harness (JMeter-based fan-in simulator + our tracing hooks) and a perf dashboard template. Estimate 2 engineer-days to wire it up and run Phase A. For Phase B we'll need a one-time infra ramp to reserve the dedicated pool — ~3–5 business days for provisioning and validation if they want reserved nodes.

Next steps I recommend we propose to BrightData:
A) Phase A (Hosted quick-proof) — 2-week engagement, Redwood to provide test harness, priority routing config, and performance runbook. We'll run the 72-hour steady test and share the dashboard. Cost: minimal (time only) and uses their existing Hosted trial credits if available.

B) If Phase A shows tail risk for priority or they insist on guaranteed sub-50 ms p95, propose Phase B Dedicated trial — include pricing options for 2x A100-equivalent reserved pool and a cheaper 4x A10-equivalent option.

I'll draft a short technical appendix and a one-page pilot statement of work (SOW) you can send with the Phase A ask. Jasmine — if you want, I'll attach the SOW draft and the harness plan for your review before you send to Tom.

Marcus Lin
